charts.name: Absolute variance columns (time series)
charts.purpose: The absolute difference between a compared scenario (AC, continuing as FC) and a baseline scenario (PL/BU/PY) per period, drawn as columns rising or hanging from a zero line and coloured by business impact.

variance_colouring.by: business impact (good_direction of the measure), not raw sign

minuend_scenario_fills.treatment: Variance columns carry the scenario notation of the compared value (the minuend): solid impact-coloured fill when it is AC, hatched when it is FC, and outlined in the special case where the minuend is PL.

sources.note: stated in the absolute-variances subsection (p.52); verified 2026-08-29

notation.title_block: required (variance titles name the comparison, e.g. "ΔPL")

geometry.zero_line: rendered across the plot at value 0
geometry.value_axis: spans the variance range; zero need not sit at the bottom

series.notes: One baseline scenario plus at least one compared scenario.

derived.compare: first non-null per period among [AC, FC]
derived.baseline: PL (default; BU or PY where PL absent)

anti_patterns: Colouring variance bars by scenario instead of by impact.
Colouring by raw sign when the measure's good direction is 'down' (e.g. cost).

charts.name: Bar chart with variance tiers
charts.purpose: The two- or three-tier bar chart: grouped bars (AC centred, the reference 1/9 of the row height above and behind) on the left, and to their right, sharing the rows, the variance tiers — ΔPL as impact-coloured bars and ΔPL% as pins — each on a 0.3 em semantic axis in the reference scenario's notation with its caption above (CO 4.2 places secondary tiers to the right of a chart with a vertical category axis; notation manual 3.2 replaces speedometers by "two-tier bar charts with variances if comparing categories"; template 5.2).

notation.tier_captions: ΔPL / ΔPL% above each tier's axis
notation.semantic_axes: each tier's zero line is a 0.3 em band in the reference scenario's notation
notation.integrated_legend: scenario names above the first row

data_labels.placement: beyond the bar; signed in the variance tiers

geometry.tier_widths: the base tier takes two parts of the width, each variance tier one, with 10-unit gaps (house-style)

citations: Notation manual 2.0 3.2 Chart replacement; 5.2 Structural comparison chart with variances — two-tier bar charts with variances; template with grouped bars, pins and variance bars

charts.name: Column chart with variance tiers
charts.purpose: The multi-tier report chart: ΔPL% pins topmost, ΔPL columns beneath, the base measure at the bottom — every period aligned vertically so what, Δ and Δ% read as one glance (CO 4.2 places secondary tiers above column charts).

notation.tier_labels: ΔPL / ΔPL% beside each tier's zero line
notation.base_tier: The base tier is a grouped column chart (notation/geometry.yaml scenario_grouping, manual 3.3 and template 5.1): the compared AC/FC column centred, the baseline (PL by default) the same width 1/9 of the category width to the left and behind it, further reference scenarios (PY) as scenario triangles, scenario abbreviations as integrated legends. A month with a baseline but no compared value still shows its frame. show_baseline: false draws the compared value alone, centred.
notation.tier_captions: ΔPL / ΔPL% left of each tier's zero line, at axis height (manual 3.6)
notation.semantic_axes: each tier's zero line is a 0.3 em band in the reference scenario's notation (manual 1.9)
notation.past_future_separator: 0.1 em medium-grey line through every tier (template 5.1)
notation.value_axis: omitted when data labels are shown and fit
notation.base_tier_labels: With show_data_labels, the base tier labels the frontmost value in each month, clearing the tallest mark (so never across the plan frame); the set is dropped with a warning if any two would touch.

geometry.base_axis: always starts at zero (enforced by the renderer); the scale spans the baseline as well as the compared values
geometry.scenario_grouping: as notation/geometry.yaml scenario_grouping (1/9 category width, compared column centred)

notation.totals: reference total at the top in its scenario notation, compared total at the bottom, both labelled with the entity (option total_label, default Total)

data_labels.placement: in the direction of the contribution, signed; totals plain and bold

notation.connectors: 0.03 em black lines at each closing level

charts.name: Contribution bridge (baseline to actual)
charts.purpose: Bridges from the baseline total (outlined, in the baseline scenario's notation) through per-period impact-coloured variance steps to the compared total (solid) — "how did we get from plan to actual".

notation.minuend_scenario_fills: FC-sourced steps hatched in the impact colour (UN 4.1)
notation.totals: baseline total outlined per its scenario; compared total solid — except on a rebased bridge, which labels the totals instead (see geometry.rebase)
notation.value_axis: omitted when data labels are shown — the labels carry the values, so axis, ticks and gridlines are redundant (SI 3.1); the unit stays in the title

geometry.columns_never_cut: the value axis always spans zero and every column in full, totals included — no zoom to the action zone, no axis break, no break glyphs; a supplied axis min/max can widen the range but never narrow it past the data (CH 1.1)

rebase.when: the steps together (lowest to highest running level) would span less than 15% of the plot height on a zero-based axis — too small to discern
rebase.axis: the horizontal axis coincides with the start value of the first change (the baseline total); only the steps are drawn, floating from it
rebase.totals: no total columns (so none is cut); the baseline total is labelled alongside the left end of the axis line ("PL 12000"), and the closing level runs out past the last step at axis weight with the compared total labelled alongside its right end ("AC 12140")
rebase.value_axis: none — the scale no longer starts at zero, so no numbers are shown on it; steps are always labelled, whatever show_data_labels says
rebase.label_scaling: K/M/bn display scaling follows the step sizes, not the totals, so steps never round to 0.0K; the end labels share that scale
rebase.room: when a falling step closes on the lowest level, space is left below the axis line for its label

anti_patterns: Zooming the axis to the steps and cutting the totals with break glyphs — every column is drawn in full (CH 1.1); rebase and label the totals instead.
Showing value-axis numbers on a rebased bridge — its scale does not start at zero.

charts.name: Relative variance pins (time series)
charts.purpose: The percentage deviation of a compared scenario from a baseline per period, drawn as pins (thin stems with a head) from a zero line, coloured by business impact.

variance_colouring.by: business impact (good_direction of the measure), not raw sign

geometry.pins: thin vertical stem from the zero line to the value, with a compact head

pin_heads.scenario_fill: The head carries the scenario notation of the compared value (the minuend): solid dark for AC, hatched for FC — per UN 4.1's relative-variance subsection (pp.54–55).

geometry.zero_line: rendered across the plot at value 0

series.notes: One baseline scenario plus at least one compared scenario.

derived.compare: first non-null per period among [AC, FC]
derived.baseline: PL (default; BU or PY where PL absent)
derived.uninterpretable: Baseline missing, zero or negative, or compare value missing. Per UN 4.1 the standard's treatment is to display "N/A" (its example is a positive value against a negative reference); hatchmark draws no stem, places the head at the zero line, and labels "N/A" when the compare value exists, and skips the period entirely when it does not.

anti_patterns: Rendering relative variances at full (absolute) column width.
Colouring pins by scenario instead of by impact.
citations: IBCS 2.0 UN 4.1 — pins for relative variances, impact colouring; audited 2026-08-29

charts.name: Stacked area chart (accumulation)
charts.purpose: Segments accumulated as stacked areas over many periods (notation manual 3.1 progression / accumulation, 3.5 "areas (stacked lines)"): the value of each segment inside its band at every period, totals on top, assisting lines marking the categories, 0.3 em non-semantic markers on the segment boundaries, and the segment names beside the last period.

notation.segment_fills: a grey ramp from measured-dark to measured-light, hatched where the value is forecast
notation.markers: 0.3 em non-semantic markers at the segment boundaries (manual 3.5)
notation.assisting_lines: 0.03 em lines at each period from the stack top to the axis

data_labels.placement: centred within the band at each period (the first and last moved inward onto the band); totals above

notation.integrated_legend: segment names right of the last period at each band's centre

citations: Notation manual 2.0 3.1; 3.5 Line and area charts — areas (stacked lines) — assisting lines indicate categories; labels for totals on top; integrated labels centred within segment; 0.3 em diameter for non-semantic markers; integrated legends centred within segment

charts.name: Stacked bar chart (accumulation)
charts.purpose: A measure across structure categories split into segments that add up (notation manual 3.1 accumulation, 3.4 "stacked bars"): each row stacks its segments from the axis, values inside the segments, totals at the end, and the segment names above the first bar centred on its segments.

notation.segment_fills: a grey ramp from measured-dark to measured-light, in the scenario notation of each value

data_labels.placement: centred within the segment; totals 0.3 em beyond the bar end

notation.integrated_legend: segment names above the first bar, centred within its segments (manual 3.4)
notation.value_axis: none — the labels carry the numbers

citations: Notation manual 2.0 3.1; 3.4 Bar charts — stacked bars — 1.5 em rows; integrated legends centred within segment; labels for totals at the end; no value axis

charts.name: Stacked column chart (accumulation)
charts.purpose: A measure over time split into segments that add up — the "accumulation" cell of the chart selection matrix (notation manual 3.1). Each column stacks its segments from zero; the value of every segment is written inside it, the total on top, and the segment names stand beside the last column as an integrated legend, so no value axis and no external legend are needed (manual 3.3 "stacked columns").

data_labels.placement: centred within the segment (white on a dark solid fill, ink otherwise, on a ground plate over a hatch); totals 0.3 em above the stack; a segment too small for its number is left unlabelled

notation.integrated_legend: segment names right of the last column, each at its segment's centre
notation.value_axis: none — the labels carry the numbers (manual 3.3)
notation.past_future_separator: 0.1 em medium-grey line between the last actual and the first forecast period

geometry.default_height: square-ish (ratio 1.0 of the nominal width, 120–170 units) so segments have room for their labels

series.notes: One segment per series LABEL; several series with one label (AC then FC) make a segment that switches scenario at the actuals boundary.

charts.name: Waterfall (cumulative contributions)
charts.purpose: Period contributions accumulated as floating columns with hairline connectors, closing on a total column, so the reader sees both each step and where the steps lead. Forecast-sourced steps render hatched.

data_labels.format: signed for deltas, plain for totals

notation.value_axis: omitted when data labels are shown — the labels carry the values, so axis, ticks and gridlines are redundant (SI 3.1); the unit stays in the title; unlabelled waterfalls keep the axis

geometry.connectors: hairline at each closing level between adjacent columns
geometry.end_total: Appended by default as the closing RESULT of the last period (manual 3.3 basic waterfall): a full column from zero drawn in the last period's own category, offset 1/9 of the category width to the right of that period's contribution and painted behind it, in the notation of the scenario the last contribution came from; its value is written inside the column (white on a solid fill, ink on a hatched one) when it is tall enough, else above or below it. No Σ category (changed 2026-10-28).
geometry.columns_never_cut: the value axis always spans zero and every column in full — no zoom, no axis break, no clipped column; a supplied axis min/max can widen the range but never narrow it past the data (CH 1.1)

series.notes: Values are per-period deltas; compare order merges AC then FC.

anti_patterns: Cutting columns with a zoomed or broken axis — every column is drawn in full from its true start (CH 1.1).
Showing value-axis numbers alongside data labels — the same values twice (SI 3.1).
Colouring deltas green/red by sign — a waterfall of a measure is scenario notation, not variance notation.

rules.title: A bullet graph needs a target or reference series
rules.statement: A bullet graph — the gauge replacement — requires a target/reference series (e.g. PL) alongside the measure; without it the bands and bar have nothing to compare against.
rules.rationale: The whole point of a bullet graph is measure-versus-target in context; a bare bar in bands communicates nothing a plain bar would not.
citations: IBCS 2.0 EX 2.2 — v2 audit 2026-08-29: bullet graphs appear nowhere in the standard — EX 2.2 replaces gauges with bars/columns; the bullet form itself is Few's design
Few, Information Dashboard Design — bullet graph design

rules.title: Avoid pseudo-3D chart effects
rules.statement: Three-dimensional chart effects distort size perception and add no information; use the flat equivalent of the same chart type.
rules.rationale: SI 2.1 groups pseudo-3D with frames and shades as decoration to remove; perspective makes identical values render at different apparent sizes.
citations: IBCS 2.0 SI 2.1 — avoid frames, shades and pseudo-3D; audited 2026-08-29

rules.title: Replace pie, ring, radar, gauge, funnel, spaghetti and filled-map charts
rules.statement: Pie and ring charts, radar charts, gauges/speedometers, funnel charts, spaghetti charts and coloured areas in maps hide the comparisons that bars, columns and lines make visible; replace them with the standard's bar, column, stacked-column, line or small-multiple forms (notation manual 3.2: pies by bars to a reference or stacked/normalised columns; speedometers by two-tier bar or column charts with variances or variance small multiples; radar by bar-chart small multiples; funnels by line charts of conversion rates over time; spaghetti by line-chart small multiples or indexed lines; map areas by bubbles, dots, columns or bars on the map, or two-tier bar charts).
rules.rationale: Circular forms permit only one-dimensional reading and waste space on a single value; EX 2 lists them as the inappropriate chart types to replace. The standard's own narrow exception (tiny pies positioned on maps) does not apply to ordinary report pages.
citations: IBCS 2.0 EX 2 / EX 2.1 / EX 2.2 — replace inappropriate chart types; pies/rings and gauges/speedometers named explicitly; audited 2026-08-29
Notation manual 2.0 3.2 Chart replacement — funnel charts, spaghetti charts and coloured areas in maps, each with its replacement

rules.title: Planned and forecast data carry their semantic fill
rules.statement: Series representing fictitious (PL/BU) or expected (FC) scenarios must be visually distinguishable from measured data by their fill treatment: outlined for plan/budget, hatched for forecast.
rules.rationale: Scenario notation lets the reader tell measured from planned from expected data at a glance, without a legend.
citations: IBCS 2.0 UN 3.2 — audited against v2 PDF 2026-08-29

rules.title: A scale group shares one measure and unit
rules.statement: Charts opted into one scale group render on a single shared value scale; that is only meaningful while every member shows the same measure in the same unit.
rules.rationale: Shared scales exist so identical visual heights mean identical values (CH 4.1, CO 5.1); mixing units inside a group makes the shared scale a lie.
citations: IBCS 2.0 CH 4.1 / CO 5.1 — identical scales for comparable charts on a page; audited 2026-08-29

rules.title: Small multiples need several panels
rules.statement: Small multiples exist to compare several same-scale panels of the same measure; with a single panel the chart is just an ordinary chart.
rules.rationale: One panel defeats the device — add a series per segment (region, product, entity) so the comparison the layout promises actually exists. All panels share one scale.
citations: IBCS 2.0 CO 5.1 / CH 4.1 — shared-scale requirement audited 2026-08-29; the min-panels check is ours

rules.title: Stacked charts do not mix positive and negative values
rules.statement: Stacked (and 100%-normalised) column or bar charts must not contain both positive and negative values across their series.
rules.rationale: With mixed signs the stacked segments no longer sum visually — the total the reader perceives is wrong. Split the measures or use a different chart.
citations: IBCS 2.0 EX 1.1 (stacked column charts) — audited 2026-08-29; the standard also cautions against >~5 series and puts the series of central interest on the axis — candidate future rules

rules.title: A variance chart needs a baseline scenario
rules.statement: Variance charts (absolute, relative, contribution) require at least two scenarios — a compared series (typically AC) and a baseline (typically PL, BU or PY) — to compute a variance.
rules.rationale: A variance is a comparison; with a single series there is nothing to compare against and the chart cannot mean anything.
citations: IBCS 2.0 UN 4.1 — section verified 2026-08-29; the check itself is definitional, not a stated rule

rules.title: Value axes start at zero
rules.statement: Value axes must not be cut: they generally start at zero (CH 1.1, as required by ISO 24896). The standard's one stated exception is indexed data (index period = 100%) with small variances, provided category labels sit at the 100% line. Variance charts are not an "exception" — they inherently include the zero baseline, so they are never truncated in the first place. Waterfalls are not exempt either: their steps float, but the axis still starts at zero and every column, totals included, is drawn in full — a waterfall column is never cut. A contribution bridge whose steps are too small to see rebases instead: its axis moves to the start value, but it then draws no total columns and shows no value scale (the totals become labels), so nothing is cut or misread.
rules.rationale: A cut axis misrepresents the underlying values — differences read far larger than they are.
citations: IBCS 2.0 CH 1.1 — audited against v2 PDF 2026-08-29; exemption list beyond indexed charts is our check pragmatics

notation.description: Cross-chart geometry: the em unit, category widths, axis chrome, line weights, variance panel proportions, scenario grouping, small-multiples grid behaviour, and reference-level devices.

em.meaning:
Font-size based dimensioning (manual 1.1): the most frequently used font size on a page is the generic font size "em", and every other dimension — line weights, label distances, category widths, pin and marker sizes, row heights — is expressed as a multiple of it, so a change of font size rescales every visual in proportion.
derived_from: the manual sizes a chart from its data, so em is NOT fixed by the pixel box a caller asks for. The reference renderer draws every chart in a NOMINAL canvas where em = 6.5 units and each category has its em width (category_widths_by_period: 3.0 em months, 3.5 quarters, 4.0 years, 2.5 weeks; 1.5 em rows on bar charts), then the SVG viewBox maps that canvas onto the requested pixels. A wider render of the same data therefore has proportionally larger type and heavier ink; a chart asked for with no size renders at its natural size (scale 1). Decided 2026-10-28 (manual recommendation taken), 0.7.1. The manual's generic sizes per page type are recorded in notation/layout.yaml (10 pt written reports and dashboards, 12 pt slides); the conversion is 1 pt = 1.333 px at 96 ppi.

sources.note: the em concept and the pt/mm/px conversion table

category_width.meaning: Columns/bars for ABSOLUTE measures (currency, quantities) are 2/3 of the category width (leaving 1/3 spacing for a single series); RELATIVE measures (ratios, percentages) are half that — 1/3 of the category width.

sources.note: v2 presents this as ISO 24896 required notation but cites no ISO clause numbers; the donor code's 'ISO 24896 §4.5.1' could not be verified — cite UN 3.1
two thirds for absolute, one third for relative, with figures

category_widths_by_period.meaning: Category widths in em for the time period types on a column chart (manual 3.3, 3.5, 3.6: 4.0 em years, 3.5 em quarters, 3.0 em months, 2.5 em weeks) and the row height of a bar chart (1.5 em, manual 3.4, 3.7). When charts of different period types share a page, the longer the period the wider its category: the manual's relations are 85% from one type to the next finer (2.2). The reference renderer still takes the pixel box the caller asks for and sizes em so that every category has exactly this width in the nominal canvas (see em.derived_from), so a chart's type and ink always stand in the manual's proportion to its columns.

sources.note: widths read off the annotated figures; the 85% relations are the bracketed house choice

line_widths.meaning: Data series lines are 0.1 em (manual 1.9), in dark, light or medium grey. The standard's thin line for relative measures (UN 3.1) is kept at half that; the manual tabulates only the one weight. Decision 2026-10-28: keep the half weight for relative measures for now.

sources.note: data series lines 0.1 em, dark, light and medium gray
thin lines for relative measures

scenario_line_markers.meaning: Lines are solid; the scenario notation is carried by the LINE MARKERS (manual 2.3 "apply the pattern to line markers in line charts"): 0.7 em squares centred on the category, solid dark for AC, solid light for PY, outlined for PL/BU, hatched for FC (manual 3.5 "lines with few data points"). Lines with many data points carry no markers and rely on selective labelling of current, extreme and end values; the reference renderer draws markers for up to 24 periods. Non-semantic markers (on stacked areas) are 0.3 em. The earlier dash mapping (long dash for PL/BU, short dash for FC) is withdrawn: it was the donor's convention and the manual carries scenario identity in the markers instead.

sources.note: markers with scenario notation, 0.7 em diameter; 0.3 em for non-semantic markers; 0.1 em line

axis_style.value_axis: omitted when data labels are shown
axis_style.meaning: Standard axes are 0.1 em, black (manual 1.9), with 0.1 em tick marks (manual 3.5). Value axes with grid lines are avoided where possible by placing data labels close to the components (manual 1.4), so every chart that shows its data labels omits the value axis, its ticks and its gridlines, and the unit stays in the title; a chart whose labels do not fit keeps the axis (SI 3.1 for waterfalls since 0.6.5, all charts since 0.7.0). Gridlines, when an unlabelled chart draws them, stay the faint house-style hairline.

sources.note: standard axes 0.1 em black; avoid value axes with grid lines where possible

separator_line.meaning: Scenario separator lines (manual 1.9): a vertical 0.1 em medium-grey line on the category axis between the last actual and the first forecast period — "separator between past and future" (3.3, 3.5, 3.6). On a multi-tier chart it runs through every tier (template 5.1). The manual names the grey without a value; #808080 is ours.

sources.note: scenario separator lines 0.1 em medium gray; separator between past and future

mark_strokes.meaning:
ONE stroke weight for every fill treatment on a bar or column body, on pin heads and line markers, and for the axis: 0.1 em (manual 1.9, "borders for bars, columns, pin-heads and line-markers 0.1 em dark gray"), the same number as axis_line_width, so a column's foot and the zero line are a single band of ink rather than two weights meeting. The border colour is the measured-dark grey, the axis black.
painted_extent: an SVG stroke straddles its path, so a mark drawn at the raw geometry paints half the stroke beyond it on every side. THREE edges are inset by half the stroke so the painted extent equals the geometry — the top edge sits at the value reported, and the painted width keeps the 2/3 category ratio of UN 3.1. The fourth, the edge resting on an axis, is deliberately NOT inset: its stroke stays centred on the axis line so the two coincide exactly. Which edge that is depends on the mark — the foot of a positive column, the top of one hanging below zero, the left of a bar growing rightward — and marks that float between two values (waterfall steps) have no baseline edge and keep all four insets.
glyph_*: pin heads and line markers once kept heavier or lighter weights of their own; the manual gives them the same 0.1 em as the bars, and at 0.7 em across they carry it.

sources.note: borders for bars, columns, pin-heads and line-markers: 0.1 em, dark gray
the three-edge inset exists to keep the category-width ratio and the zero baseline honest

assisting_lines.meaning: Assisting lines (tying designations to components, difference markers) and waterfall connection lines are 0.03 em, black (manual 1.9).

sources.note: assisting lines and waterfall connection lines 0.03 em black

label_distance.meaning: Legends and labels can label a component in all four directions and keep 0.3 em from it (manual 1.5). Data labels sit on top of columns and at the end of bars, legends beside the components they identify; both are always horizontal, never rotated (manual 1.4).

sources.section: 1.5 Typography — alignments and distances of legends and labels
sources.note: 0.3 em in all four positions

pins.head_shape: square, in the compared scenario's notation
pins.meaning: Relative variances are pins: a 0.3 em shaft and a 0.7 em head carrying the notation of the scenario compared (solid for AC, hatched for FC), in the impact colour of the variance (manual 3.6 / 3.7). Pins are scaled independently of the underlying measure, but every relative variance chart on a page uses the same scale.

sources.note: 0.3 em width of pin, 0.7 em diameter, pin heads with semantic scenario notation

hatch.tile: axis-aligned square of side pitch × √2, stripes drawn explicitly (no patternTransform)
hatch.meaning:
The forecast hatch: stripes at 45 degrees leaning "/" — rising left to right, the SAME lean in bars and columns. The stripe carries the mark's own stroke weight and the perpendicular pitch is 2.2x that, giving roughly 45/55 ink, so the texture stays in proportion to the outline containing it at any INK_W.
tile: the stripes are drawn explicitly inside an axis-aligned square tile (the main diagonal and the two corner pieces of its neighbours) rather than as a rotated tile: rasterisers such as cairo leave the corners of a rotated tile transparent, which let the ground show through and broke the texture into a checker (0.7.0).
ground: the space between the stripes is painted opaque in the background colour (colors.background), never left transparent. A hatched mark is a column in its own right, so where a forecast stands in front of an outlined plan frame (scenario_overlap) it hides the frame behind it, exactly as a solid actual does; nothing shows through the stripes.
UN 3.2 states the MEANING (forecast is outlined AND hatched, and the stripes take the colour of measured data) and nothing about geometry. The numbers are measured off three independent figures: Fig UN 3.2-3 (p.46, 255ppi) and Figs UN 4.1-1 / UN 4.1-4 (pp.50/53, 200dpi) all give perpendicular stripe 0.89-1.02pt on pitch 1.87-1.92pt, and the 45 degree lean is exact — one pixel left per pixel down in the native raster. Note the legend swatch on p.44 is drawn coarser than the charts on p.46 at the same raster scale, so the standard is not self-consistent here either; the chart figures are modelled, not the swatch. The notation manual's figures are too small to settle the lean; decision 2026-10-28: keep "/".

sources.note: p.45 states forecast is outlined and hatched and that stripes take the measured-data colour; no angle, width or spacing is given anywhere
angle, stripe and pitch measured at native raster resolution 2026-09-19 — figure-derived

scenario_grouping.integrated_legend: scenario abbreviations beside the first column (FC beside the last), at the value's height
scenario_grouping.meaning:
A scenario comparison in one category (manual 3.3 "grouped columns", 3.4 "grouped bars"): every column the SAME width; the compared scenario — AC, or FC where no actual exists yet — is CENTRED in its category segment at 2/3 of the category width; the reference column (PL by default) is offset 1/9 of the CATEGORY width to the left and painted first, so the measured figure stands in front of an outlined plan frame. The manual's offset is of the category width, not the bar width, and the compared column, not the pair, is centred: both differ from every earlier version of this entry (a figure-derived third of the bar width capped at 5 units up to 0.6.5, a strict 20% of the bar width in 0.6.6–0.6.8), which are withdrawn.
sequence: scenarios of the identical period are arranged PY – PL – BU – FC – AC, left to right on a horizontal category axis and top to bottom on a vertical one (manual 2.3), which is also the paint order — so where FC and AC share a category, FC sits 1/9 left of the centred AC. Scenarios of DIFFERENT periods are arranged in temporal ascending order.
second_reference: a second reference scenario is not a third column but a scenario triangle in its own notation — a light-grey solid triangle for PY, an outlined one for PL — pointing at the compared column from the left (from above on a bar chart) at the reference's value height (manual 3.3 / 3.4 "scenario triangles for second reference scenario with semantic notation"). The reference drawn as a column is the caller's baseline when it is present, otherwise PL, then BU, then PY.
data_labels: only the frontmost column in a category carries a value, placed 0.3 em above the TALLEST mark in the category (the longest on a bar chart), so the number never crosses the plan frame's top rule.
integrated_legend: the scenario abbreviations are written beside the first column carrying each scenario, left of it at the value's height, and FC beside the last forecast column on the right (manual 1.4 "legends close to the components they identify", 3.3, template 5.1); on a bar chart the reference is named above the first row and AC below the last (3.4).
On a horizontal chart the arrangement rotates: the reference sits 1/9 of the row height ABOVE the compared bar and behind it; triangles point down; the label clears the LONGEST bar in the row.

notation.description: Report types, page layout settings, the generic font size per page type, the layout of messages, titles, subtitles, annotations and legends.

report_types.exploratory: supports active data analysis; located BEFORE the analysis in decision support; no message
report_types.message: communicates the findings of analyses as messages or stories; located AFTER the analysis; the visuals prove the messages

formats.written_reports: must speak for themselves; exploratory or message reports
formats.presentations: verbal reports delivered in person; the author's interpretations and messages are essential; exploratory visuals may support
formats.dashboards: interactive electronic exploratory reports; may carry message elements as annotations; need a business-responsive design (convert and remove less important information rather than moving visuals to secondary pages; convert bar charts to table columns before removing them)

notation.description: Label decorations for analytic period treatments, plus the period-span convention.

ytd.meaning: Year-to-date accumulation ending at this period.

ytg.meaning: Year-to-go — the remainder of the year from this period.

moving.meaning: Moving (annual) analysis ending at this period.

average-temporal.meaning: Temporal average (YTD/moving averages): the ∅ is APPENDED to the notation (UN 4.2). The donor code used a prefix-only 'average' mode — corrected after the v2 audit.

average-structural.meaning: Structural average: the ∅ may be appended or used as a prefix (UN 4.3); hatchmark uses the prefix form.

first-day.meaning: Value as at the first day of the period (opening balance).

last-day.meaning: Value as at the last day of the period (closing balance).

span.meaning: A time span between two period labels — exactly two full stops, no blanks, and deliberately not a typographic ellipsis.

notation.description: Data scenarios and their visual encoding. All scenarios share one base hue; the FILL TREATMENT (not colour) carries the scenario distinction, because colour is reserved for analytical meaning.

AC.name: Actual
AC.meaning: Figures that have actually occurred in the current period.
AC.manual: Measured data, e.g. Actual — solid dark (64, 64, 64)

PY.name: Previous Year
PY.meaning: Measured figures from an earlier comparable period.
PY.nuance: Per UN 3.2, the lighter fill applies when earlier periods appear in SCENARIO COMPARISONS; in a pure time series, earlier measured periods need not be lightened. (The donor codebase lightened PY always.)

PL.name: Plan
PL.meaning: Planned figures agreed for the period.
PL.mnemonic: Fictitious (planned) data is an empty frame that "fills up when materialising".

BU.name: Budget
BU.meaning: Budgeted figures; visually identical treatment to Plan.

FC.name: Forecast
FC.meaning: Expected figures, extrapolated from measured data.
FC.nuance: Per UN 3.2, the hatch stripes are drawn in the colour of measured data.

sequence.different_periods: temporal ascending order, left to right (horizontal axes) or top to bottom (vertical axes)
pattern_applies_to: axes in charts showing variances (reference scenario)
pin heads in charts using pins for relative variances
the line below column headers in tables

variance_reference_default.meaning: When a variance chart names no reference scenario, it is measured against the first of these the dataset carries: against plan when the dataset has a plan, else against the previous year, else the budget. A dataset with none of them still reports ΔPL, all N/A, so the gap is visible rather than silent. The renderer's `defaultBaseline` mirrors this list.

sources.note: variances are shown against PL in the time-series templates and against PY in the structure waterfall (template 5.3, 3.7); the order is ours

principles.text: Scenario identity is encoded by fill treatment (solid / outlined / hatched), never by introducing a new hue. AC and PY are solid (dark and light); PL and BU are outlined; FC is hatched. The standard gives grey only as an example base hue — an organisation may use another base hue so long as it is consistent.

principles.text: Colour is used only for analytical meaning (SI 2.2); green/red/blue are assigned to variance semantics (UN 4.1). Scenario series must not introduce hues that would collide with that meaning.

rows.column_header: abbreviations (AC, PL, ΔPL%); separated from the body by a 0.1 em dark-grey line, replaced by 0.3 em semantic lines when scenario columns are shown; multi-level headers separated by 0.1 em dark-grey lines
rows.standard: height 1.5 em; separated by 0.03 em dotted light-grey lines; no line above the top row of a set
rows.of_which: below the mother row; 0.8 em text; height 1.0 em; no separating line
rows.result: bold, below the rows of the calculation; separated by 0.1 em dark-grey lines; empty rows of 0.7 em support the structure

columns.variance: as standard columns, with a plus sign for positive variances

embedded_charts.sparklines: only when scaled properly (e.g. indexed) across the whole table; individually scaled sparklines mislead

notation.description: The boundary between house style and standard: a theme may restyle tokens the standard leaves open (impact hues in colour mode, typeface) and may never alter what the standard fixes (scenario fill treatments, the monochrome and CVD substitution schemes, notation geometry).

desirable.note: UN 4.1 fixes the semantic ROLE (and describes green); the exact hue is house style.

undesirable.note: UN 4.1 describes dark red; the exact hue is house style.

scenario-notation.reason: UN 3.2 fixes scenario identity in fill treatment (solid/outlined/ hatched) and light/dark bases. A theme changing these would change what the chart SAYS, not how it looks.

substitution-schemes.reason: The monochrome and CVD palettes are the standard's own accessibility fallbacks (UN 4.1); theming them would defeat their purpose.

geometry.reason: Bar-width ratios (UN 3.1), zero-based axes (CH 1.1) and title structure (UN 2.2) are notation, not decoration.

principles.text: A theme restyles house-style tokens; it never redefines standard notation. Every themable token knows which mode it applies in, and overrides outside those bounds are ignored by the renderer.
citations: IBCS 2.0 UN 4.1 — roles fixed, hues open

principles.text: Themed desirable and undesirable hues must remain clearly distinguishable from each other and from the scenario greys; organisations with accessibility requirements should verify their palette or rely on the CVD mode, which themes cannot alter.
